links.outcome: Run-to-run stability of LLM automated scoring (coefficient of variation) across 3 cases
links.effect: CVs were low for total scores (0.87%-1.12%) and item-level scoring (0.55%-0.73%); fully-processed system raised ICCs from 0.414/0.500 to 0.923/0.972 in moderate and complex cases versus baseline.
links.quote: Specifically, the coefficients of variation (CV) were low across total scores (0.87%-1.12%) and item-level scoring (0.55%-0.73%).

unlisted_practices: Layered design strategies (multi-step processing) to improve LLM scoring stability and human-AI consistency, tested with baseline comparisons
Evidence-based transparent rationales for automated LLM assessment
Zero-modification transfer of the evaluation framework to an alternative LLM
LLM-simulated patients for medical history-taking training

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates an LLM-based simulated patient training system with medical students, conducting systematic baseline comparisons of specific multi-level design/framework strategies to evaluate stability, human-AI consistency, and transparency.

primary.practice: dialog quality and automated assessment prompt/evaluation framework strategies
